entries.name: Airplane (airliner)
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours

source.author: weirdybeardyman
source.note: Gap filled (plan row 142 had no source). Twin-jet airliner by weirdybeardyman on OpenGameArt, CC0 per the page; the gear-up .blend (opened with auto-run off), for sky shots. entries.name: Axe (one-handed)
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 198 (Quaternius static Axe via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Axe_Small.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword entry). The pack has three axes: Axe (crescent battle-axe head with a top spike), Axe_Double (two-bladed labrys) and Axe_Small (a bearded one-handed axe); Axe_Small was taken because its single broad bearded head is the plainest axe silhouette and reads at a glance in the hero view. Height 0.75 m is the whole axe, heel to the top of the poll (a one-handed axe; the head is chunky for its size, about 0.30 m from poll to edge, as the stylized source draws it). Rest pose: upright, haft along +Y, heel on y = 0; head flat in the XY plane with the cutting edge toward +X (about 4-6 cm thick along Z). The pipeline centres the bounding box, so the haft is not on the origin: the haft axis runs at x = -0.115 m, z = 0 (its curved heel ends near x = -0.10 m). Grip (cord-wrapped) from y 0.19 to 0.43 m, hold at about y 0.27 m; bare flared heel 0 to 0.19 m; steel collar 0.52 m; head from y 0.37 (beard tip) to 0.73 m, steel poll cap 0.56 to 0.75 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by (+0.115, -0.27, 0) m in the axe's frame, then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and +X (the edge) faces the swing. Colours match the sword: head, poll and collar pale steel (moon over sky), haft amber over sky.

entries.name: Bee
entries.style: low-poly chibi, flat colours, modelled stripes (Quaternius 2021)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Wave-1 row 54 named the Bee from Quaternius's poly.pizza "Cute Creatures" set; poly.pizza is behind a Cloudflare challenge. The same author's Textured Cute Monster Pack (Aug 2020, OpenGameArt, the zip the ghost entry uses) has a Bee with the plan's four clips, but its yellow and black stripes are painted across a few large faces of the texture: flattened to flat colours (16 clusters at face UV centroids) it became a near-black blob with odd yellow patches and no stripes, which does not read as a bee. entries.name: Bicycle
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours; simple diamond-frame street bike with round tubes, no spokes, chain or pedals (Quaternius Public Transport, 2017)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Wave 1 row 130 was a gap (no bicycle in any planned source); this fills it from Quaternius's CC0 LowPoly Public Transport pack on OpenGameArt. The pack has two bikes, Bicycle and SquareFrameBicycle: the same diamond frame, wheels, handlebar and saddle, one with round tubes (2812 tris) and one with square-section tubes (1144 tris). Bicycle is used: round tubes shade as clean cel bands and read closer to a steel city bike, the square one looks boxier up close. Neither is a true mamachari (no step-through frame, basket, mudguards or chain guard); it reads as a plain street or school bike. The .blend member is used, not the FBX or OBJ: those carry only grey #e7e7e7 materials, which gltf-transform merges into one, while the .blend keeps the red frame, dark tyres, grips and saddle. Height 1.0 m to the top of the handlebar grips; then it is 1.85 m long (a 26-inch city bike is about 1.8-1.9 m), 0.47 m wide, wheels 0.60 m across. Front wheel toward +Z (yaw 180), both tyres on y = 0. For a rider (metres, model space): saddle top at (0, 0.89, -0.31), the saddle spans z -0.45 to -0.17; handlebar grips at (+-0.19, 0.975, 0.455), each grip spans |x| 0.14-0.24; front hub (0, 0.30, 0.62), rear hub (0, 0.30, -0.62); bottom bracket (crank axle) at about (0, 0.29, -0.34). Pedals and cranks are not modelled: put the feet at about (+-0.12, 0.12-0.46, -0.34 +- 0.17) on a 0.17 m crank circle around the bottom bracket. Static, no clips; wheels are separate nodes (FrontWheel, BackWheel) in the GLB.

entries.name: Row boat
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Watercraft Kit)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Kenney boat-row-large (GLB with the kit colormap), same kit and fetch pin as boat-fishing and boat-sail. Chosen over boat-row-small (all-wood, stubby 1.9:1 hull, two cramped seats): the large one has a painted hull with wooden gunwale, thwarts and oars, a 2.4:1 hull and room for a rower and a passenger. Height 1.19 m (keel to the raised oar grips) gives a 4.0 m hull and 2.0 m beam (chunky toy proportions, beam on the wide side); that is about 0.85x the kit scale of boat-fishing/boat-sail, which would make it a 4.7 m boat. Bow (the narrow end with a small foredeck) faces +Z. y = 0 is the flat hull bottom; the chine is at y = 0.45 m and the waterline sits at about y = 0.3 m, so a film sinks the boat 0.3 m into its water plane. Floor y = 0.34 m (z -1.67..+0.79); gunwale top y = 0.90 m; seat tops y = 0.56 m, 0.66 m either side of x = 0: middle thwart z -0.45..+0.04 (rower, facing -Z), stern seat z -1.67..-1.18 (passenger, facing +Z), and a foredeck at the same height z +0.79..+1.61. Seats sit only 0.22 m above the floor (toy depth), so a sitting character's legs go forward along the floor. Rowlock blocks on the gunwale at y 0.79 m, z -1.0..+0.45; the two oars (one source object, 'paddles') rest shipped up and outboard at z -0.37..-0.80, blades down near the water, spanning 3.86 m. Cream hull, red gunwale, thwarts, foredeck and oars (the source wood), dark-brown floor. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Bookcase
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Quaternius Furniture Pack)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Substitutes for the plan's Quaternius bookcase (poly.pizza static GLB, blocked by a Cloudflare challenge) with the same author's CC0 Furniture Pack on OpenGameArt: `BookCaseBooks`, from the .blend (the pack's FBX and OBJ carry only grey placeholder materials, so all seven import as one colour). A five-shelf bookcase with a stepped crown and plinth, every shelf filled with upright and leaning books. The Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0 route used for sofa and desk-teacher was tried first: none of its bookcases (bookcaseOpen, bookcaseOpenLow, bookcaseClosed, bookcaseClosedWide, bookcaseClosedDoors) holds books, the kit's `books` is a separate 15 cm stack, and the pipeline cannot combine two members into one static model. KayKit Furniture Bits (free tier) has no shelf. Sized to a real bookcase: 1.80 m tall, 0.89 m wide, 0.53 m deep, in metres like desk-teacher (0.74 m) and sofa (0.89 m), so they stand together at one scale. The pack's `BookCaseLargeBooks` is a wider variant. Colours: the sides and back (source `DarkWood`) are noon's dark brown so the books stand out; the shelves, crown and plinth (`Wood`) are the paper wood with a light shade so shelf edges read against the back; the four cover materials get their own pairs (red, pink, cream, near-black) and the page edges a pale pair. Front (open shelves) faces +Z after a -90 degree yaw. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Wooden bow
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Quaternius 2018), chunky stylized limbs

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Wave-1 row 197 named Quaternius's static 'Bow' on the poly.pizza CDN, which is blocked (Cloudflare challenge). This is Bow_Wooden.fbx from Quaternius's LowPoly Medieval Weapons pack on OpenGameArt (CC0 on the page), very likely the same wooden bow. No free Japanese yumi was found: OpenGameArt 3D search for 'yumi' had nothing; KayKit Adventurers (672074b) and Skeletons (15b62b9) ship only crossbows, arrows and quivers. Candidates rendered and rejected: Bow_Wooden2 (same pack, stiffer stepped limbs), Quaternius RPG Characters Ranger_Bow (spiky fantasy bow with a big hand guard) and tbbk's Low Poly Composite Bow (CC0, clean recurve but 1 cm deep, so it turns into a hairline in cel). Orientation: standing upright on its lower tip, string vertical; the arrow direction is +Z (back of the bow towards +Z, string at -Z), so the left view shows it broadside with the back to image-left and the front view shows it edge-on. Grip: the red-wrapped section at mid-height, about 0.6-0.8 m up (centre ~0.7 m), on the bow's centre line; the string runs between the nocks just inside the two tips.Shipped at 1.4 m tip to tip, a short recurve-style hunting bow (real bows 1.2-2 m); the limbs are chunky and stylized, so it reads as a game/fantasy bow, not a slender longbow or yumi. Static, no clips. Colours (indigo): wood in iris over sky with threshold 0.1 so only the undersides shade, the leather grip in accent, the string in moon.

entries.name: Bush
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, stacked faceted leaf mounds (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static bush on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is Bush_2 from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip as the tree, tree-pine and tree-autumn entries, so they read as one set. Of the four bushes in the pack (Bush_1, Bush_2, BushBerries_1, BushBerries_2) it has the roundest footprint (1.2 x 1.2 m; Bush_1 is an elongated 1.1 x 1.4 m) and no berries, so it works as a plain garden shrub or hedge piece. The mesh is a closed solid, so it is not double-sided. Height 1 m: a garden shrub, azalea or a clipped hedge clump along a park path is 0.8-1.2 m, about hip to waist on a 1.6 m person. Colours on meadow: leaves a rounded mid green (iris) shading to deep green (hair), lighter than the ink, so the clump reads darker and fuller than the light-green grass beside it. Its unused Berry material (no faces in Bush_2) maps to leaves. Static: no clips.

entries.name: Butterfly
entries.style: low-poly card wings (CDmir 2015, 240 tris): a monarch, its photo texture flattened to flat colours: orange wings with dark tips and a dark body; real size: the rest pose lies with wings spread flat, so a 1 cm rest height gives a 7.9 cm wingspan (a monarch is about 9-10 cm, a garden butterfly 6-10 cm)

source.author: Čestmír Dammer (CDmir, TinyWorlds)
source.note: The plan's own source (gaps list: butterfly, OGA butterfly-animated). license.txt in the zip: Čestmír Dammer, CC0; it adds that the diffuse texture was derived from photo documentation by Rick Hoppmann. Only flat per-face colours sampled from that texture survive in the GLB. The texture flattens to 7 clusters: the orange, yellow and ochre wing faces plus the black #202021 wing-base faces -> wing; #212121 (body, legs and hindwing edges), the brown forewing tips #7b6219 and the untextured remainder -> dark, so it reads as a monarch: orange wings with dark tips. Height 0.01 m is the rest pose with wings flat (legs to wing plane), which makes the wingspan 7.9 cm, inside the real 6-10 cm. Clips: Flying -> fly (0.42 s flap loop, ground clamped: the wings sweep below the body on the downstroke, and the clamp lifts the body as a real downstroke does); Sitting2 (perched, wings closed upright) -> sit and the preview pose; Sitting1 (perched, wings folded back flat) kept under its source name. Both sitting clips are single poses.

entries.name: Cactus
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, a smooth saguaro column with two upturned arms (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static cactus on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is Cactus_3 from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip and pin as the tree, tree-palm, lilypad and other plant entries, so they read as one set. Of the ten cacti in the pack (Cactus_1-5, CactusFlower_1, CactusFlowers_2-5) it is the classic saguaro: one tall column with two upturned arms on opposite sides, a clean silhouette at a glance. Cactus_1 is an armless spiny barrel, Cactus_4/5 and CactusFlowers_4/5 are prickly-pear pads, CactusFlower_1 is a wide agave-like rosette, Cactus_2 has three stubby arms bunched on one side, and CactusFlowers_2/3 are saguaros with spiky pink crowns that turn into noise at a distance. Height 3.5 m: a saguaro starts growing arms at roughly 2-4 m (desert-film saguaros run 3-6 m); at 3.5 m it stands about twice a 1.6 m person, the arms springing at 1.7-2.2 m. The arms lie in one plane, so ingest.yaw -64 turns that plane to face between the front and hero cameras: the arms spread in the front, three-quarter and hero views (only the side views see them end-on). Colours on meadow: the body is iris (mid green) shading to hair (deep green), a saguaro's own colour. Smooth, one material, no spines. Static: no clips.

source.author: Quaternius

Of the pack's three clouds (all rendered) it reads best as a puffy cumulus: a big central lobe with a smaller puff on each side over a flat base, the classic anime cloud profile, where Cloud_1 is two lumps and Cloud_3 a long sloping mound. The broad side faces +Z (the front view shows the three lobes); y = 0 is the flat bottom. Size: a sky prop, 15 m tall, about 25 m wide and 15 m deep; real cumulus are hundreds of metres across, so a film places it far off or scales it (uniform scale keeps the base flat). Colours on indigo: sclera white shading to moon pale blue, with ink. noInk was tried too: without the hull the lobes merge into one white blob and the cloud reads as a lump, so the ink stays (it also draws the creases between puffs). Shade threshold 0 (default 0.35): at the default half the cloud went blue in patches; at 0 the shade sits on the underside and the far side, the flat-bottomed anime cumulus look. entries.name: Computer
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Substitutes for the plan's Quaternius computer (poly.pizza static GLB, blocked by a Cloudflare challenge). Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0, three kit pieces built into one static model with `ingest.attach` (no bone): `computerScreen` (a flat monitor on a short neck and a trapezoid foot, screen tilted back), `computerKeyboard` centred in front of it with a small gap (offset [0.0555, 0, 0.178] kit units: the keyboard file's origin is its back-left corner, the screen's its back-left too) and `computerMouse` to the keyboard's right, level with its middle (offset [0.39, 0, 0.1615]). The kit's `laptop` (screen and keyboard in one) was rendered as the alternative and reads clearly as a laptop, but the plan row is a desk computer. Quaternius's CC0 Furniture Pack on OpenGameArt (used for bookcase) has no computer. Normalised by the monitor: the model's height is the monitor's top, 0.45 m with its foot (keyboard and mouse are lower), so the screen is 0.60 m wide (a 27-inch screen), the keyboard 0.43 m wide and the whole set 0.63 m wide, 0.43 m deep; that is 0.79x the kit's own scale (where desk-teacher is 0.74 m), since at kit scale the monitor would stand 0.57 m tall and 0.76 m wide, oversized next to that desk. The set is centred on its bbox, so the monitor sits about 1.5 cm left of x = 0. A debug render placed the source materials: bezel, sides, back shell and foot are `metalDark`, the screen face and the neck `metal`; the keyboard body `metalDark@computerKeyboard`, its two key blocks `metalMedium`; the mouse `metalDark@computerMouse` (the optimizer merges the three identical `metalDark` materials into one, so they share a role anyway). The mouse's rounded back renders as a small ink-dark cap in the cel look (clay shows clean geometry and the source winding is consistent; `doubleSided` does not change it), which reads as a dark palm end at film sizes. Keyboard body and mouse take the case pair and the key blocks the screen's dark brown in one tone, so the keys read as two dark panels on a pale board. As for the TV entry, the screen is the script's dark brown (`iris`, lighter than ink so the outline stays distinct) in one tone, and the case takes the pale paper pair (practical, sky shade), so the dark screen sits in a clear light frame; this reads as an off or dark screen, not a lit one. Front (screen) faces +Z. Static, no clips.

source.author: Quaternius

Each blade is a closed solid (a thin prism), not a one-sided card, so it is not double-sided. 192 triangles, cheap to instance. Height 0.25 m: a tuft of unmown lawn or verge grass is 0.2-0.3 m, ankle to mid-shin on a 1.6 m person; footprint about 0.2 x 0.27 m. Colours on meadow: leaves a fresh light green (line) shading to mid green (iris), lighter and brighter than the bush's mid-to-deep green so the two read apart, with the leaves threshold lowered to 0 so the lit tips read light green over mid-green bases (at the default most of each thin blade fell into shade). Static: no clips.

entries.name: Acoustic guitar
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours

source.author: MonoTone
source.note: Plan row q-guitar-5fp8gpomrb pointed at poly.pizza (blocked). Candidates rendered: KayKit Mixed Bag 1 (free, CC0) guitar_A/guitar_B is a Flying-V electric (same mesh, two colours), not acoustic, so it was rejected; MonoTone's Classical Guitar on OpenGameArt (CC0 on the page) is a properly modelled nylon-string classical: slotted headstock with six tuners, 18 frets, six strings, rosette, tie-block bridge, a real sound hole with an interior. The FBX ships upright with the soundboard toward +X, so yaw -90 turns the sound hole to +Z; no pitch/roll needed. Rest pose: upright, neck up, the bottom of the body (end block) on y = 0. Height 1.0 m is the whole instrument (a real classical guitar is 0.97 to 1.0 m); lower bout 0.41 m across X (real ~0.37 m, slightly generous), body depth about 0.1 m. Landmarks: body from y 0 to about 0.52 m (neck joint and heel at about 0.52 m, back side), sound hole centre at about y 0.34 m, bridge at about y 0.17 m, nut at about y 0.84 m, headstock 0.84 to 1.0 m. Grip: fretting hand on the neck, y 0.55 to 0.82 m; strumming hand over the sound hole on the +Z face, y 0.25 to 0.38 m; the lower bout rests on the right thigh with the waist at about y 0.3 m. A classical guitar has no strap buttons: for a strap, tie to the end of the body (y 0, back centre) and to the heel (y 0.52 m, -Z side). Colours on noon: spruce top paper tan (shade skin, threshold -0.5 so the soundboard stays lit from the front), sides and back accent red-brown shading to iris (the sound-hole interior reads dark iris), neck/fretboard and bridge iris, binding and rosette, frets, nut/saddle/tuners pale moon, strings practical white. Strings, frets and trim are drawn without ink: their hulls otherwise turned the fretboard into a black slab and gave the sound hole a jagged rim. Static: no clips.

source.note: Plan row #143 was a gap (no helicopter in any planned pack). Uploaded to OpenGameArt by brylie from Sketchfab (https://sketchfab.com/models/0c4d0167c739469a992b5dab8fde510f); the page's licence is CC BY 4.0 and its attribution notice and the zip's AUTHOR file name blueskinrulez (https://sketchfab.com/blueskinrulez). Candidates checked: whitaker's 'Simple Helicopter' (CC0) is an ASCII FBX, which Blender cannot import; drummyfish's helicopter.obj from '32 low poly models' (CC0) is 194 triangles in one mesh with no materials (one flat colour, rotor fused to the body). Size: 3.6 m tall to the rotor hub, 10.2 m long nose to tail fin, main rotor about 9 m across (a light twin such as an EC135 is 3.5 m tall, 10.2 m long, 10.2 m rotor). Noon script: the source's yellow body goes to accent red over iris shade, its red stripes and hub to cream (moon over sky), skids and tail parts iris over line, rotor blades and windows near-black (line over ink). Faceted (smooth false). No tail rotor in the source. ROTOR: the source's own clip 'Take 01' (mapped to fly, looping, 0.417 s) turns the four main blades (nodes Cube.003-Cube.006, Cube003-Cube006 in three.js) and the hub (Cylinder.004) a quarter turn about the mast, so the loop is seamless for a four-blade rotor; play it faster (scale the time) for a faster spin. The blade nodes' origins are NOT on the mast (the clip animates translation and rotation together), so spin the rotor with the clip rather than by rotating the nodes yourself.

The painted texture is flattened to 16 clusters: the five browns (cap top and gills) -> cap; the two creams (cap spots, teeth and the eye catchlights, which fall in the paler one) and the untextured #e7e7e7 -> spot; the five olive greys (the stem body and face) -> body; the near-black cluster (eye discs, mouth rim) and the dark olive cluster (lower eyelids) -> dark; the two plums (mouth cavity and tongue) -> tongue. The source's olive-grey stem and brown cap are recoloured to a pale stem under a vermilion cap with cream spots, so it reads as a toadstool at a glance; the spots are whole faces, so they come out as blocky patches, not round dots. dark has threshold -0.6 so the eyes stay mostly solid. Ground: like the ghost and demon it is a stem-shaped body on a flat base, no legs; Walk and Jump hop off the ground by design (up to 13 and 22 cm), Death sinks up to 11 cm as it tips onto its cap and HitRecieve 2 mm as it rocks, so both clamp to the ground. Substituted with umask007's 'Ork' (orc barbarian) on OpenGameArt, a single Blender 2.68 .blend licensed CC-BY 3.0 only (checked on the page, Oct 2026); umask007's attribution instructions say the base mesh is based on Clint Bellanger's 'Base Human Models (low poly)' (OpenGameArt, CC-BY 3.0) and the face on a MakeHuman model. Opened only through the pipeline with auto-run off. The file ships six weapons on the rig; five of them (Axe, Bow, GreatSword, Hammer, Sword) are hidden from render in the file and are removed by the pipeline, so the one kept is the Hellebard (halberd), already bone-parented to hand_L, plus the ShoulderArmor on brust_L and the Schaerpe (shoulder strap). The skin has one packed 256 px baked texture (green skin with the eye whites); in Blender 4.2 its face-image link is lost, so the pipeline samples it for every material of the body mesh, which only over-splits the materials: every split maps back to its source material's role, and the white cluster of the skin is the eye whites. Coloured on the meadow script so the orc keeps its classic green skin (line #a9d16e over an iris #3f8a47 shade); everything else stays off the greens so it reads apart from the skin: the topknot, belt, boots and halberd haft are ink with a deep-green (hair) shade, the loincloth panel, sash and haft butt accent red, the skirt sides and shoulder armour moon over a sky shade, the halberd blade and steel plates sclera over sky, the teeth sclera over a practical-yellow shade, the eye whites sclera. Every texture cluster keeps its source material's role. Clips: kept 8 of 14 with keepActions. Dropped the four dualWield clips, spell and the one-handed attack: they were made for the hidden one-handed weapons and swing the halberd by one hand or push it through the body. Kept attack2h2 as attack (the full overhead chop), attack2h and attack2h3 under their names, die as death (ground clamp: the fall sinks up to 16 cm otherwise), flinch as hit, howl (raises the halberd overhead), walk and run (in place). There is no idle clip; the rest pose is a T-pose, so the views and the `stand` pose use flinch at 0 s, a neutral stance with the halberd upright. Centring: the rest pose is a T-pose with the halberd pointing forward, so x/z are centred on the body mesh alone (ingest.centerOn: Ork); height and floor still count everything.

Rest pose: upright, snath along +Y with a gentle S-curve and a hooked foot on y = 0; blade flat in the XY plane (about 2 cm thick along Z), mounted by a collar at y 1.40 to 1.60 m, curving out toward +X and down to its tip at (+0.46, 1.33) m, with the concave cutting edge facing down toward the user and a short back spike to -X. The pipeline centres the bounding box, so the snath is not on the origin: its axis runs at z = 0 and x = -0.37 m near the foot, -0.28 m at mid grip and about -0.33 m along the bare upper shaft (y 0.85 to 1.40 m). The cord-wrapped grip runs from y 0.10 to 0.80 m. Two-handed hold: lower hand at about (-0.37, 0.25, 0) m, upper hand at about (-0.28, 0.70, 0) m; a one-handed carry (reaper pose) takes the upper hand point. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by minus that hand point in the scythe's frame (e.g. (+0.28, -0.70, 0) m for the upper hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and +X (the blade) points forward over the shoulder or out to the side. Colours match the sword: blade and back spike pale steel (moon over sky), snath, grip wrap and collar amber over sky.

source.author: Quaternius

Colours match the sword and axe: rim and rivets pale steel (moon over sky), wood planks amber over sky; the source's white paint is mapped to the script's red accent (paint), since white paint against the pale steel rim lost the quartering. entries.name: Ocean liner
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Watercraft Kit)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Kenney ship-ocean-liner (GLB with the kit colormap), same kit and fetch pin as boat-fishing. A four-funnel Titanic-style liner, stylized and stubby: the toy is only 2.4 times as long as it is tall, so no single scale is real. Height 70 m keel to mast tops (the funnel tops sit at about 62 m; a modern cruise ship stands about 70 m) gives a 167 m hull and a 37 m beam: short for a liner (real ones run 200 to 300 m) but a believable length for a smaller ocean ship, and beam and height read right at the far/mid distances films place it. Bow toward +Z (image-left in the lab left view; the funnels rake aft). y = 0 is the keel; the waterline sits at about y = 11.5 m (the top of the red boot-topping, where the dark hull band starts), so a film sinks the ship 11.5 m into its water plane. Cream superstructure, dark-brown hull band, funnel tops, masts and rigging, buff funnels (White Star style), red boot-topping and flags. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Spear
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 199 (Quaternius static Spear via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Spear.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries). Height 2.0 m is the whole spear, butt to point (a common infantry or hunting spear is 1.8-2.2 m). Rest pose: upright, point at +Y, butt on y = 0; the leaf-shaped head is flat in the XY plane (edges along X, about 0.10 m wide, 2 cm thick along Z). The pipeline centres the bounding box; the shaft axis runs at about x = -0.003 m, z = 0 (the stylized shaft wobbles: it drifts to x = -0.017 m near y 1.0 m and the butt kinks to x = +0.04 m below y 0.1 m). Cord-wrapped lower grip from y 0.16 to 0.60 m (rear hand at about y 0.35 m); bare shaft above it (lead hand for a two-handed thrust at about y 0.95 m, axis x = -0.017 m); a second binding from 1.39 to 1.61 m under the head; steel head 1.61 to 2.00 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by (+0.003, -0.35, 0) m in the spear's frame (or (+0.017, -0.95, 0) for the lead hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and the point faces the thrust. Colours match the sword and axe: head pale steel (moon over sky), shaft and both cord bindings amber over sky (the bindings read by their ink rings).

entries.name: Speeder craft
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Space Kit)

source.author: Kenney

entries.name: Spider

source.author: Quaternius

Scale it up in a film if it should be a monster. Colours on the noon script: brown body #5c3d32 with near-black shade (threshold 0 so the shade sits on the underside and leg undersides only), accent-red eyes. Ground: every clip is clamped (Spider_Walk and the flip onto the back in Spider_Death sink a leg tip 1 mm; the rest never sink).

entries.name: Wooden staff (crook)
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2017)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 201 (Quaternius static Staff via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is WoodenStaff.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Lowpoly RPG Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence CC0 on the page). Three candidates were rendered: this one (a plain unpainted wooden staff with a squared crook at the top), umplix's CC0 'Low-poly Staffs' Wooden Staff (a thick square shaft with a kink and a claw holding a floating crystal; with the crystal dropped the claw reads as broken) and KayKit Adventurers staff.gltf (an ornate mage staff with a ring head and bands). None is a straight bo; this crook is the plainest well-modelled wooden staff and matches the sword, axe and spear author. Height 1.7 m is the whole staff, foot to the top of the crook (a quarterstaff or walking staff is 1.5-1.8 m); the shaft is stylized thick, about 7.5 cm across. Rest pose (ingest.yaw 90): upright, foot on y = 0, the crook flat in the XY plane: the shaft bends out to x = -0.20 m at y 1.45 m, the crook tops out at y 1.70 m and its tip curls back toward +X (to x = +0.20 m at y 1.35-1.60 m); about 9 cm thick along Z. The pipeline centres the bounding box; the shaft axis runs at about x = 0.00 to +0.015 m, z = 0 (the stylized shaft wobbles: about +0.02 m at y 0.35 m, 0.00 at 0.60 m, +0.015 m at 0.95-1.05 m). Two-hand quarterstaff grip: lower hand at about y 0.55 m, upper hand at about y 1.05 m. To put it in hands: parent to the lower hand, offset by (0, -0.55, 0) m in the staff's frame (or (-0.015, -1.05, 0) for the upper hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction; as a walking staff in one hand use the upper-hand offset with the foot planted. Colours match the sword, axe and spear wood: amber over sky.

entries.name: Palm tree
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, curved segmented trunk under a crown of faceted fronds (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius

Of the four palms in the pack it has the fullest crown (more than a dozen fronds, 5.2 x 4.7 m) on the classic S-curved coconut-palm trunk; PalmTree_3 is straighter and thinner-crowned, PalmTree_4 has only eight fronds, and PalmTree_2 leans so far that its base sits 3.5 m off the crown's centre. The fronds are closed shells (a doubleSided render was identical), so they are not double-sided. Its Coconuts material is buried in the crown and never shows, so it maps to trunk. Height 8 m: a coconut palm on a beach or resort promenade is 6-10 m when young to mid-age (old ones reach 20-30 m); at 8 m the fronds spring from about 7 m and droop to 5.5 m, high over a 1.6 m person, as in an anime beach or island background. Colours on meadow: fronds the mid green (iris) shading to the deep green (hair), a richer green than the willow's light foliage; the trunk is pale skin-tan shading to vermilion (accent). Meadow has no brown: of its non-green pairs, skin over accent gives the clearest two-tone on the thin trunk and the warmest, closest read of a sun-bleached palm trunk (skin over practical and practical over skin barely separate, and moon over skin is the willow's trunk). entries.name: Udon bowl

Normalised to 0.094 m tall (the chopsticks top), which makes the bowl 0.083 m tall and 0.195 m across the flats (0.225 m corner to corner); the chopsticks are 0.245 m long

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Wave-1 row 191 named a Quaternius static model on poly.pizza (Cloudflare challenge, off limits). Kenney Food Kit (same pinned zip as cake and onigiri) has no noodle, ramen or udon member; its bowls are `bowl` (empty), `bowl-cereal` (orange cereal, spoon), `bowl-broth` (purple band, egg halves, a fried-tofu slab, a green garnish) and `bowl-soup` (white hexagonal bowl, pale broth, scallion flecks and three thick loops standing out of the broth). `bowl-soup` is used: its loops read as thick udon noodles once coloured white. Unlike the `ramen` entry (red bowl, dark-orange broth, egg, chashu, upright wooden chopsticks): a white bowl with a brown band, pale dashi broth, white noodle loops, brown scallion flecks and red lacquer chopsticks lying flat. Colours (noon): bowl and inner wall practical with a moon shade; band iris; broth sky with skin shade; noodle loops (their colour cluster also covers the thin broth ring at the wall, which reads as bowl) practical with moon shade; scallions iris (noon has no green); chopsticks accent with iris shade, threshold -0.5. Size: normalised by total height; the bowl across the flats (x) is the 0.18-0.2 m dimension. Round-ish, no facing. Static, no clips.

entries.name: UFO (flying saucer)
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, colour map flattened (Kenney Tower Defense Kit)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: The plan's pack (Kenney Tower Defense Kit, zip pinned by sha256), but `enemy-ufo-c` instead of the plan's `enemy-ufo-a`. All four kit saucers (a, b, c, d) were rendered: a is squat with a raised turret collar, b has a green bumper ring, d is a stacked double disc; c is the classic flying saucer (a wide, thin faceted disc, a raised ring and a big dome) and reads best. Also compared Quaternius Ultimate Spaceships (May 2021, OpenGameArt, used by the `spaceship` entry): its only disc ship, Pancake, is a gunship with a fighter cockpit, not a classic saucer. Real size: a film flying saucer is about 8-12 m across; at a 5.2 m rest height (dome top) this model is 9.9 m across. Bottom of the belly at y = 0 (films lift it). Kenney ships every triangle twice, back to back, so `ingest.dropBackfaces` removes the inward copies (440 -> 220 tris); otherwise their ink hulls paint the surface black. The colour map is flattened to 5 colours: silver disc panels -> hull (moon over sky), the purple disc panels and rim -> lights (indigo accent red over sky), the darker raised ring and belly -> metal (line over sky), the white dome and its collar -> dome (practical amber over iris, a lit canopy for a night sky). Kept faceted (`smooth: false`). Static, no clips.

entries.name: Umbrella
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (KayKit)

source.author: Kay Lousberg (KayKit)
source.note: Plan row gap-umbrella said no source had an umbrella (procedural). KayKit Mixed Bag 1 (Sept 2026) has one: umbrella_pink.gltf from the free tier on itch.io (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0, credit optional). The pack ships one umbrella shape in four colours (pink, blue, green, yellow); pink was taken because it maps straight onto the script's red accent, the classic anime rain umbrella. It is OPEN: an eight-panel scalloped dome with a top ferrule, a straight shaft and a J-hook handle; the canopy is modelled with an inner surface, so it is not doubleSided. Rest pose: upright, canopy up, the bottom of the hook on y = 0, shaft on the y axis. Height 0.9 m is the whole umbrella, hook to ferrule (a real full-size umbrella is 0.85 to 0.95 m long); KayKit's dome is deeper and its shaft shorter than a real one, so the canopy is 0.86 m across X (0.81 m flat-to-flat along Z) where a real one is about 1.0 m; scale 1.15 for a full-size canopy. Canopy rim at about y 0.48 m, shaft meets canopy at about y 0.52 m. The hook curls toward +X in the XY plane, its tip at about x 0.18 m, y 0.16 m. Grip: the straight wooden handle just above the hook, y 0.11 to 0.21 m on the shaft axis (hold at about y 0.17 m). To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by -0.17 m along the umbrella's Y, then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction (canopy above the head). Colours on indigo: canopy accent red, handle iris amber, shaft and ferrule moon pale steel, all shading to sky; canopy shade threshold 0.1 (default 0.35 shaded half the dome). Static: no clips.

entries.name: Windmill
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney City Kit Industrial 2.0)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: The plan row (#156) as given: Kenney City Kit Industrial 2.0 windmill.glb. It is a MODERN three-blade wind turbine (tower on a wider base, nacelle, hub, three blades), not a traditional mill, and stylized stubby (rotor diameter about half the height). Alternatives checked: the same kit's windmill-low (a stubbier turbine; reads less well), and for a traditional mill the Kenney Fantasy Town Kit 2.0 windmill.glb, which is only the four-sail lattice cross meant to sit on a building (no tower or cap, one mesh), so not a stand-alone windmill; no Quaternius pack already pinned in the library (Ultimate Nature, Ultimate Textured Buildings, Farm Animals, Furniture, Platformer and the rest) has a windmill. Height 60 m to the top blade tip (real turbines are 60-150 m to the tip; the low end because the chunky proportions read small: the tower is about 5 m wide and the base about 9 m at this scale); the hub (rotor centre) is at y = 43.5 m. Rotor faces +Z (ingest yaw 90). SPINNING THE ROTOR: blades and hub are a separate node named blades (three.js: root.getObjectByName("blades"), a Group of the rotor meshes with their ink hulls). Its origin is NOT the hub (gltf-transform quantization folded an offset and a 0.563 scale into the node): rotate it about its parent's (node windmill) X axis through the parent-frame point H = (-0.2404, 1.6764, -0.0008); in the model frame at 60 m that is the axis +Z through (0.06, 43.47, 5.90) m. Each frame, from the rest values p0 and q0: r = Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle((1, 0, 0), angle); blades.quaternion = r * q0; blades.position = r(p0 - H) + H. Noon script: tower, nacelle and blade roots moon over sky shade; the source's yellow base, nacelle collar and grey blade tips all go to accent (vermilion) over iris shade, threshold -0.2 so the long blade tips stay mostly lit (red-tipped blades, as real turbines are marked); hub iris, flat. Faceted (smooth false), 456 tris. Static, no clips.

source.note: Wave-1 row 104 named the Quaternius Zombie from 'Animated models (misc)' on poly.pizza (now behind a Cloudflare challenge). Substituted with Zombie_Male from the Quaternius Ultimate Animated Character Pack (Nov 2019) on OpenGameArt (same zip and pin as man-casual and worker). Chosen over Zombie_Female in the same pack: the male's open skull with the brain showing, bare scalp, scowl and torn shirt read as a zombie at a glance, while the female's long hair hides the face and the head wound. It ships the pack's 11 clips (idle, walk, punch, hit, sit, walk-carry, pick-up, one-handed shoot, victory, defeat, stand-up), not the misc set's 8 (no run, jump or death). The source skin is green; no colour script has a green, so it is painted indigo's cold moon-white (bloodless, corpse-pale) with red eyes, brain and guts. Alternative: Kenney's blocky mini character-zombie (Kenney kits, CC0), not used: far less modelled.
